item.title: Vehicle left road and struck flats – recurring safety risk at Ravensbourne Rd/Ringers Rd, 25th August
item.description:
At about 2:30am on 25 August, a large van rolled off the carriageway at the junction of Ravensbourne Road and Ringers Road, crossed the pavement/verge and struck the flats. The impact also knocked down the Ravensbourne Road street sign and posts. I recovered the sign and am keeping it safe for Council collection. This is not the first time a vehicle has left the road at this location. Fortunately no pedestrians were present, but the consequences could have been very serious at a busier time. Please treat this as more than a street-furniture repair and ask Highways/Road Safety to inspect the junction and consider protective measures such as bollards, kerbing or other suitable barriers to prevent vehicles rolling down Ringers Road reaching the pavement and residential buildings.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 12, Ringers Road, Plaistow, Greater London

item.title: Long pothole on cyclist turning line, 25th August
item.description:
This pot hole has been bad for a year and getting worse. It’s the direct line cyclist use to turn down Vanbrugh Park Rd. It is very busy with cars behind, buses pulling in and cars trying to over take buses in the exact line that the bikes are turning on. The bikes have right of way. Not fixing this could result in a significant injury to a cyclist. Even better please add a turning lane and bike route to protect cyclists more on the turn. It is a very popular route to Greenwich Park
